title: Using complex prompts to identify fine-grained biases in image generation through ChatGPT-4o
findings: The study found that using complex prompts with ChatGPT-4o and DALL-E 3 resulted in images of pastors that were uniformly White and male. This homogeneity is theorized to result from the generated scenarios lacking 'socially marked' contexts that the AI associates with non-White pastors (e.g., the Civil Rights movement). A pilot study with the older ChatGPT-3.5 model showed a different bias, where it disproportionately assigned non-White demographics (specifically Black individuals) to negative vignettes about pastors, while positive vignettes heavily favored White individuals. The paper suggests ChatGPT-4o's 'fix' for this text-based bias was to implement an unrealistic, randomized demographic distribution, which the more complex image-generation prompts seemed to circumvent, defaulting back to a homogeneous representation.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured stereotypical racial representation of the religious role 'pastor' in AI-generated vignettes and images. It specifically investigated the underrepresentation of non-White pastors and the association of different racial demographics with positive versus negative scenarios.
